ip_top_stories.title: Publishers Step Up AI Copyright Fight as SPUR Coalition Adds 30 New Members
ip_top_stories.summary: The SPUR coalition, which campaigns for publisher rights in the AI era, has expanded by 30 new members including leading Canadian news organisations. The coalition is pushing for licensing frameworks and fair compensation as AI companies continue to train on news and publishing content without authorisation.

ip_top_stories.title: Can AI Author Copyrightable Work? The Supreme Court Just Declined to Say Yes
ip_top_stories.summary: The US Supreme Court declined to rule that AI-generated work is eligible for copyright protection, leaving the question unresolved. The decision maintains the existing position that copyright requires human authorship, with significant implications for AI content creators and the broader industry.

ip_top_stories.title: UK Directs Google to Strengthen AI Search Attribution and Provide Publisher Opt-Out Controls
ip_top_stories.summary: The UK's Competition and Markets Authority has imposed new rules requiring Google to improve attribution in AI-generated search results and give publishers meaningful opt-out controls over their content being used in AI Overviews. The rules represent a significant regulatory intervention in the relationship between AI search tools and news publishers.

ip_top_stories.title: Still Facing Copyright Lawsuits, AI Music Generator Suno Raises Another $400M
ip_top_stories.summary: AI music generation platform Suno has raised a further $400 million in funding despite ongoing copyright litigation from major music labels. Separately, rival platform Udio has asked a court to seal the size of its AI training dataset in Sony Music's copyright case, citing competitive harm.

ip_top_stories.title: Rewriting EU AI and Copyright Rules Puts €600 Billion at Risk, New Study Warns
ip_top_stories.summary: A new study warns that proposed changes to EU AI and copyright rules could put up to €600 billion in AI-related economic value at risk. The findings are being cited by tech industry groups in opposition to moves to revise the EU's text and data mining copyright exemptions.

ip_further_links.title: US Judge Sides with Meta in AI Training Copyright Case
ip_further_links.summary: A US judge has ruled in Meta's favour in a copyright case concerning the use of published works to train AI models, a significant development in the ongoing legal battles over AI training data.

ip_further_links.title: After Suno, Udio Asks Court to Seal the Size of Its AI Training Data in Sony Music's Copyright Case
ip_further_links.summary: Udio has requested that a court seal details about the volume of its AI training data in Sony Music's copyright lawsuit, following a similar move by Suno, with both companies citing competitive harm.

ip_further_links.title: Sony Invests in AI Copyright-Protection Firm Midnight Labs
ip_further_links.summary: Sony has made a strategic investment in Midnight Labs, a firm developing AI-powered copyright protection technology for creative content.

ip_further_links.title: Exclusive: Bipartisan Members Introduce New Bill to Protect Creators from AI Style Theft
ip_further_links.summary: Bipartisan US legislators have introduced a new bill aimed at protecting creators whose artistic styles are replicated by AI systems without consent or compensation.

ip_further_links.title: Björn Ulvaeus Addresses AI, Copyright and Licensing
ip_further_links.summary: ABBA co-founder and music rights advocate Björn Ulvaeus has publicly addressed the challenges AI poses to copyright and music licensing frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: China Puts AI Copyright Violations in Crosshairs of Annual Anti-Piracy Campaign
ip_further_links.summary: China has included AI-related copyright infringement as a priority target in its annual anti-piracy enforcement campaign, signalling increased regulatory scrutiny of AI training and content practices.

ip_further_links.title: USBS 2026: Publishing CEOs Warn Against AI 'Witch Hunt' [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Publishing industry CEOs speaking at the US Book Show 2026 cautioned against an overly punitive approach to AI use in publishing, even as copyright debates intensify.

ip_further_links.title: NYT's Sulzberger Condemns AI Giants for 'Brazen Theft of Intellectual Property'
ip_further_links.summary: New York Times publisher A.G. Sulzberger has publicly condemned AI companies for what he describes as the brazen theft of intellectual property, intensifying the media industry's pushback against AI training practices.

ip_further_links.title: ARIA, APRA AMCOS Heads Respond to Calls for Pro-AI Copyright Overhaul
ip_further_links.summary: The heads of Australian music industry bodies ARIA and APRA AMCOS have pushed back against calls to overhaul copyright law in favour of AI developers, defending existing protections for creators.

ip_further_links.title: California's AB 412 Still Demands Developers Do The Impossible
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of California's proposed AI transparency bill AB 412 argues that its training data disclosure requirements are technically unworkable for AI developers as currently drafted.
